title: Quick quiz: how a home battery works
intro: Ten questions on the technology. Tap an answer to see why.
messages: Worth another read of the guide above.

qs.q: What does a home battery do?
options: Stores electricity so you can use it later
Cuts the voltage from the grid
qs.why: It charges from the grid or from solar and gives that power back when you need it.

qs.q: On a battery, what does the kWh number tell you?
options: How much energy it can hold
qs.why: kWh is the size of the tank. kW is how quickly power can come out at once.

qs.q: Does every home battery keep your lights on in an outage?
options: No, it needs backup-capable wiring and a gateway
Only if you also have solar
qs.why: Some batteries only shift power to save money. Ask the installer how the system switches to backup.

qs.q: You make more solar power at midday than you use. A battery can:
options: Store the extra for the evening
Sell it back at triple the price
Turn it into heat for the roof
qs.why: Without a battery, extra solar goes to the grid. With one, you use it yourself after sunset.

qs.q: Which chemistry is common in new home batteries?
qs.why: Lithium iron phosphate is popular for its safety record and long life.

qs.q: How can a battery save money under time-of-use rates?
options: Charge when power is cheap and use it when power is costly
Run all night at full power
qs.why: Rates are lower off-peak. A battery moves your use out of the expensive hours.

qs.q: Through an outage, which is easier for one battery to run?
options: Electric dryer, oven and central air at once
qs.why: Big heating and cooking loads drain a battery fast. Many homes back up a few essential circuits.

qs.q: Where should a home battery go?
options: Where the maker allows, within its temperature range and clearances
qs.why: Check the installation manual. Heat and cold both shorten battery life.

qs.q: How long a warranty do many home batteries carry?
qs.why: Ten years is common, often with a promise to still hold a share of its capacity.

qs.q: A battery has 90 percent round-trip efficiency. What does that mean?
options: Put in 100 kWh and get about 90 kWh back
qs.why: Some energy is lost as heat when charging and discharging.
